title: The Pilgrims of the Journey to the West
text:
In Wu Cheng'en's great novel, the monk Tang Sanzang was sent from China to India to bring back Buddhist scriptures. He was gentle, devout and almost helpless, so the bodhisattva Guanyin gave him companions, each a former troublemaker working off a punishment.

Sun Wukong, the Monkey King, was brilliant and brave, able to cover a vast distance in one somersault and change into seventy-two forms, but he was also arrogant and quick to kill. Zhu Bajie, the Pig, was strong but greedy, lazy and always ready to give up and go home. Sha Wujing, the quiet former river monster, carried the luggage and kept the peace. A dragon prince, turned into a white horse, carried the monk.

They quarreled constantly. Bajie stirred up the master against Monkey. Once Tang Sanzang, unable to see through a shapeshifting demon, sent Monkey away in anger, and the group nearly came to ruin until he was brought back. Yet each member was needed. Monkey saw through disguises, Bajie fought in the water, Sha held the group together, and the monk's steadiness gave them a purpose.

After eighty-one ordeals they reached the West, received the scriptures and carried them home.
lesson: A team does not need members who get along easily. It needs members whose different strengths fit the task, and a shared purpose strong enough to survive their quarrels.
people: Tang Sanzang, Sun Wukong, Zhu Bajie, Sha Wujing
source: Wu Cheng'en (attributed), Journey to the West (Xiyou ji)
